biological.citation: Circadian clock protein Bmal1 accelerates acute myeloid leukemia by inhibiting ferroptosis through the EBF3/ALOX15 axis (PMID: 37271497)
biological.summary: EBF3 acts as a transcription factor that binds to the ALOX15 promoter to enhance its expression, promoting ferroptosis-mediated cell death in AML. Bmal1 suppresses EBF3 expression through EZH2-mediated promoter methylation, establishing EBF3 as a key node in the ferroptosis regulatory pathway in leukemia.
biological.sample_size: AML cell lines (HL-60, NB4) and xenograft tumor model

biological.citation: An Integrated Phenotypic and Genotypic Approach Reveals a High-Risk Subtype Association for EBF3 Missense Variants Affecting the Zinc Finger Domain (PMID: 35340043)
biological.summary: EBF3 contains a zinc finger domain (ZNF) critical for stabilizing DNA-binding interactions. Missense variants disrupting the ZNF impair transcriptional activation and fail to rescue viability in Drosophila, while variants in the DNA-binding domain (DBD) retain partial function, establishing domain-specific functional requirements.
biological.sample_size: 83 individuals with EBF3-related neurodevelopmental disorder (41 newly identified + literature meta-analysis)

biological.citation: Loss of Notch signaling in skeletal stem cells enhances bone formation with aging (PMID: 37752132)
biological.summary: EBF3 is identified as a downstream mediator of Notch signaling in skeletal stem and progenitor cells (SSPCs). Elevated Notch signaling during aging dysregulates EBF3 expression, and modulating this pathway ameliorates skeletal aging phenotypes, highlighting EBF3 as a therapeutic target.

biological.citation: A cell type-aware framework for nominating non-coding variants in Mendelian regulatory disorders (PMID: 39333082)
biological.summary: Single-cell epigenomic profiling of ~86,000 cranial motor neurons identified EBF3 as a disease gene in congenital cranial dysinnervation disorders (CCDDs). Non-coding variants predicted to regulate EBF3 were nominated in unsolved CCDD cases, establishing EBF3 as a key developmental regulator in motor neuron specification.
biological.sample_size: 899 whole genome sequences from 270 CCDD pedigrees; ~86,000 cMNs profiled

biological.citation: EBF3 reactivation by inhibiting the EGR1/EZH2/HDAC9 complex promotes metastasis via transcriptionally enhancing vimentin in nasopharyngeal carcinoma (PMID: 34906623)
biological.summary: EBF3 acts as a transcription factor that directly binds the Vimentin promoter to upregulate its expression, promoting epithelial-mesenchymal transition and metastasis. EBF3 is epigenetically silenced by the EGR1/EZH2/HDAC9 complex via H3K27-Me3 deposition at its promoter.
biological.sample_size: Nasopharyngeal carcinoma patient tissues and cell lines
biological.significance: High EBF3/Vimentin expression correlated with poor overall survival

biological.citation: Transient and lineage-restricted requirement of Ebf3 for sternum ossification (PMID: 32398354)
biological.summary: Ebf3 is a transcription factor marking tenocytes and connective tissue cells in skeletal muscle. Ebf3 knockout mice show defective sternum ossification due to impaired generation of Runx2+ pre-osteoblasts, with stage-specific requirements at embryonic day 9.5-10.5 in lateral plate mesoderm cells.
biological.sample_size: Zebrafish enhancer-trap lines and conditional/temporal Ebf3 knockout mice

biological.citation: Concurrent RB1 and P53 pathway disruption predisposes to the development of a primitive neuronal component in high-grade gliomas depending on MYC-driven EBF3 transcription (PMID: 39821672)
biological.summary: EBF3, an early neurogenic transcription factor, is directly controlled by MYC transcription factors in accessible chromatin sites. EBF3 expression is essential for the primitive neuronal component (PNC) phenotype in glioblastomas with concurrent RB1 and TP53 pathway inactivation.
biological.sample_size: High-grade gliomas with primitive neuronal component

biological.citation: Mutations in EBF3 Disturb Transcriptional Profiles and Cause Intellectual Disability, Ataxia, and Facial Dysmorphism (PMID: 28017373)
biological.summary: EBF3 is a transcription factor in the early B cell factor family involved in neuronal differentiation. EBF3 mutations cause mislocalization, reduced DNA-binding activity, impaired transcriptional activation of target genes (e.g., CDKN1A), and reduced genome-wide DNA binding and gene-regulatory activity as demonstrated by ChIP-seq and RNA-seq.
biological.sample_size: 10 individuals with EBF3 variants; HEK293T cells for functional assays
biological.significance: EBF3 variants present in ~0.1% of individuals with unexplained neurodevelopmental disorders

biological.citation: ASHG 2016 - Functional investigation of Early B-Cell Factor 3 (EBF3) haplo-insufficiency as a novel genetic cause of developmental delay and intellectual disability
biological.summary: ChIP-seq and RNA-seq experiments demonstrate that EBF3 variants reduce DNA-binding affinity and disrupt critical neurodevelopmental gene expression networks. EBF3 acts as a transcription factor controlling migration of Cajal-Retzius cells and driving expression of genes critical for neuronal differentiation.
biological.sample_size: 2 DD/ID patients with EBF3 variants; functional validation in cell culture

biological.citation: ASHG 2016 - Large-scale rare variants association studies in hereditary cutaneous and ocular melanoma uncover new risk gene with tumor suppressor activity
biological.summary: EBF3 was identified as a novel secondary candidate in an exome-wide rare variant association study of familial cutaneous melanoma (n=273) and ocular melanoma (n=99) cases, replicated in TCGA, and functionally validated as a bona fide tumor suppressor gene with tumor suppressor properties.
biological.sample_size: 273 familial cutaneous melanoma cases, 99 ocular melanoma cases, 7,629 ancestry-matched controls
